title: Publish envelope: sampled-anchor + versioned cost-lattice + runtime compatibility webhooks
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal: deliver a publishable ‘envelope’ for Redwood-verified performance profiles that bundles sampled anchor measurements, a versioned cost-lattice for hardware/seq normalization, and a lightweight runtime-compatibility webhook contract. This will enable deterministic pinning decisions and safer automated rollouts when new model versions or hardware variants are onboarded.

Background: current profile publishes contain measured latency/throughput/cost numbers but lack a canonical sample provenance artifact and a stable cost normalization primitive. That makes regional comparability, incremental pinning, and automatic fallbacks brittle. Engineering has implemented a prototype sampling harness and a draft webhook spec; PM will consolidate requirements, prioritize the cost-lattice shape, and define the publish/playback UX for console and API consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Published envelope JSON schema (v1) documented in Confluence and validated by runtime team
Sampling harness produces anchor bundles for N=1000 requests per target sequence-length bucket and signs provenance metadata
Cost-lattice normalization algorithm defined and validated across at least two hardware classes (A100, H100) with sample-backed unit tests
Compatibility webhook spec implemented (GET /profiles/:id/compat) and a staging endpoint accepting runtime capability fingerprints
Canary workflow: ability to rollback a pinned profile automatically when sampled production traces show >10% latency regression over baseline within 1 hour
Console UI surface added: profile publish modal that includes anchor preview, normalized cost estimate, runtime compatibility warnings
tasks: Finalize envelope schema and example payloads
Integrate sampling harness output with signing service (artifact provenance)
Design & implement cost-lattice normalization function and expose as service
Define and spec compatibility webhook contract with runtime (timeout, response shape, versioning)
Add profile publish flow to Console + API: preview, sign, publish, and rollback
Create automated test-suite for anchor reproducibility and cross-hardware normalization
Run pilot on 3 recently onboarded models and produce a publishability report
comments: 2026-02-16 — PM kickoff: aligned on scope with Runtime (Ravi) and Console (Maria). Decided to prioritize a minimal envelope (anchor + lattice + webhook) vs larger attestation format to unblock Q2 publishes.
2026-02-22 — Engineering note (Ravi): prototype sampling harness done. Produces anchor bundles per-seq-length and includes trace IDs. Needs signing integration and size trimming for Console preview.
2026-02-26 — Design review (Maria): suggested UX for publish modal that surfaces normalized cost per 1k tokens, sample variance band, and runtime compatibility warnings. Will mock screens next week.

2026-03-02 — PM decision: use quantized cost-lattice with 3 axes (hardware_class, seq_bucket, production_temp) to keep payload compact and interpretable. Justification: sufficient for common workloads and fast to compute in the Console.
2026-03-05 — Security review queued: signing cadence and artifact TTL documented; KMS integration planned. Security requested a threat model doc before GA — added as follow-up task.

2026-03-08 — Integration update (Liam): webhook contract PR created: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4821. Implemented handshake, version header, and a small JSON response containing supported_kv and max_context_length.

2026-03-10 — Pilot run: sampled anchors for 3 models across A100/H100. Early results: normalized cost delta stable within 6% for prompt-heavy workloads; larger variance for very long responses (seq>2048) — investigating batching/kv-cache impact.
notes: This ticket is intended to produce a minimally sufficient publish artifact that the Console, API consumers, and runtime can rely on for pinning and automated rollouts. Follow-on work will expand the attestation envelope and integrate automated decay detection.
implementation_risks: Normalization across heterogeneous hardware is non-trivial; sampling bias (time-of-day, workload mix) can skew anchors. We mitigate with stratified sampling, pilot on representative workloads, and conservative default pins.
follow_up: Create the security threat model and add a GA checklist (retention policy, signature rotation, telemetry hooks). Plan training doc for SREs on interpreting normalized cost and rollback triggers.
